riverfarm_headman_shared: We don't truck with witches here. Didn't used to, anyway.
A bad crop year, you learn to count what's yours twice. Once for the harvest, once for what walked off with it.
Sorry, I don't mean to- never mind. Long nights lately.
Wolves didn't used to come this close to the fences. Whatever's stirring up that hollow is pushing everything our way, wolves included.
riverfarm_headman_shared_2: The hollow's west past the fields. Nobody walks you there. Nobody local, anyway.
riverfarm_hunter_shared: Hollow's quieter than it should be. Doesn't sit right.
Lost two lambs to something with thorns for teeth. Wasn't a wolf.
Know that treeline better than the headman does. He'd rather not.
Wolf sign's thicker toward the hollow, week by week. They've left their own ground. Now they're on mine.
The witch? Her business is hers and I keep to mine. Sheep is my trade, all of it.

entities.observe: Fresh-turned earth, packed and raised into a long low wall. The spoil is thrown to the field side, and a boot-path runs up the near face.
entities.toast: Just raised earth. Whatever it's for, nobody's finished it yet.

entities.observe: One long thatch ridge, twice the width of any cottage. Smoke curls from a vent at the peak even in daylight.
Clay-daub walls, a low thatch roof. A washing line strung between two posts.
entities.toast: Voices on the other side of the daub, going on without you.

entities.observe: A second cottage, smaller, its thatch newer than its neighbor's.
entities.toast: The door is pulled to. Smoke comes off the roof-hole and drifts along the thatch.

entities._comment: Sails overhang above the blocked footprint. The art's own doorway sits on column 19, over riverfarm_mill_door [19,5] and the pinned approach [19,6]; [19,4] was ALREADY blocked, so art-only, no sim change.
entities.observe: Sails turning slow in whatever wind there is. The grinding floor above the wheat fields.
entities.toast: The sails creak overhead. No one's tending it right now.

entities.observe: A stone-ringed well, rope worn smooth by years of hauling. The water's clean this far from the blight talk.
entities.toast: Cool water, a long way down. You leave the rope where you found it.

entities.observe: Bundled and stacked before the rain, with the cut ends turned in.
Straw and an old coat, arms out over the tilled rows. It isn't working today — there are crows on its own hat.
A plank pier reaching out over the river. The village's whole trade with anywhere downstream starts here.
entities.toast: Weathered planks, sound underfoot. The current runs steady past the end of it.

entities.observe: Two bars and a post. The tilled rows start a stride past it.
The rail carries on east from here. A pair of sparrows lift off the top bar and settle again three posts down.

entities._comment: absent on herd_rerouted, twins at (8,9)/(9,9) present; these cells also left `blocked`/`cover_skip` (map array beats presence).
entities.observe: Low fence rail, bordering the tilled rows.
Low fence rail, bordering the tilled rows.
Rails re-set forty paces east of where they stood, and the gap they left is the corusdeer road. The hoof marks come through it three deep.
Rails re-set forty paces east of where they stood, and the gap they left is the corusdeer road. The hoof marks come through it three deep.
The top rail is rubbed bare along one stretch, and it gives a dry knock when you set a hand on it.
Low fence rail, bordering the tilled rows.
A low rail on the west boundary of the rows. Bindweed has taken the near post to the top and stopped there.

talk_pool_stages._comment: lowest priority: hollow thread and blight terminal outrank.
lines: Seed sacks came through clean. Fields'll tell come spring whether the coin was worth it. Around here that counts as gratitude.
@riverfarm_headman_shared_2
@riverfarm_headman_shared
Ledger balances. First time in three years it's balanced honest.
River's due in a fortnight and for once I know exactly what's above the line.
I've stopped recounting. Turns out that was most of the problem, {addr}.

entities.observe: A ledger under one arm, mud to the knee, the look of a man doing three jobs badly instead of one job well.

dialogue.speaker: Former Headman
dialogue.text: Not now. Got a village to hold together.

lines: Thank you. I don't think I said that right the first ten times I tried.
I keep counting days like the price is still running. Old habit. I'll lose it eventually.
Ask me again sometime, once I've had more practice sounding like myself.

entities.observe: Ordinary, except for how still they stand, and a faint red thread at the wrist that doesn't match anything else they're wearing.

@riverfarm_hunter_shared

Still don't walk that line after dark. Knowing what it is didn't make it friendly.
Two lambs I lost this spring. Whatever took them, it wasn't the thing on the line.

lines: Lambs know your step before I do. Never seen that off a stranger.
The one that limped is walking sound. I'd stopped expecting it to.
Herd at the north bend, pen full, and hands that aren't mine doing the gentling.

lines: Lambs are in before dark now, every night. Nobody argues about it anymore.
Pack's fed elsewhere or it's thinner. Either way it's off my fields.
First snow came and the count held. The count held.

entities.observe: Tar-marked hands, a crook worn smooth, wolf sign on his boots. The flock is penned. He is still watching the treeline.

entities._comment: THE VILLAGE'S ONLY EXIT (witch_hollow is a dead end off it): the gate must be met by EVERY arrival cohort. door_mounted is the one counter both the pre-fix path and portals.json's door_awakened row satisfy; gating on either attunement alone re-strands a cohort. Never tighten past the row's own gate.
entities.observe: The stone stands at the middle of the village with a spiral cut into its face, softened by weather. Attunement works like this: show a door the right stone and the door learns the place, and can open onto it ever after. The grass around its base is worn down to bare dirt.
entities.toast: Cold, plain stone, and it stays cold for you. This one has never been shown a door.

entities.observe: A narrow break in the treeline, west of the fields. The light changes past the first few trees.

entities._comment: `ally_requires{hunter_will_come:1}` is banked ONLY by data/dialogue/riverfarm_hunter.json's watch ask, at the village.
entities.observe: After dark the field's edge has eyes in it, low to the ground and catching the light. Look straight at them and they go out. They are back as soon as your eye moves off.
entities.gate_closed_toast: Stubble, a fence post, and daylight. One patch of grass lies flat, and the dew is gone off it.

visual_states._comment: Marker visible ONLY while the night encounter_when gate can fire

entities._comment: interact-only, no trigger_radius, no encounter_when gate (the corusdeer_range/razorbeak_nest unconditional shape): ungated beside the lamb pen from hour one, furniture not a threat. present_when is legal here: no trigger_radius.
entities.observe: Vines thicker than they should be, over the fence line and into the village since the thicket business settled. They creep across open ground, twitching against a wind that isn't blowing.

entities._comment: Regional repeatable work. The serving_tray idiom (once_per_waking + gold, interactions.gd's `serve:` key): takeable once a waking, forever. Counter riverfarm_field_jobs is frozen. 2 gold = half the crude_draught bronze anchor, below a Guild bounty because there is no risk in it.
entities.observe: A plank of hooks at the fence line, each hook holding a scrap with a task on it and no name. Ditching, thatch, a fence a cow disagrees with. The scraps come down about as fast as they go up.
entities.once_per_waking_toast: Every hook is bare. The board is empty till tomorrow.
entities.toast: You take a scrap off its hook and spend the morning behind it. Ditching, mostly. The village pays coin because coin is the thing it has least of, and it pays on the day.

variants.toast: Your name is chalked against a hook before you get there. The chalk comes off on your hand.
The hook you get is the one nobody else will touch: the wet corner down by the river, every time. They give it to you because you finish it.

entities.observe: The mill's ground-floor door, set into the base of the tower on the river side. The sluice hums even with the wheel pinned.

entities._comment: #330 R2 [Beast Tamer] door: base banks soothed_a_beast, the variant tended_beasts, paid in wool. #396: legacy id; A Shepherd; present ALWAYS (ruling 13), so [16,11] is now blocked like the rail cells either side of it (a present entity blocks its own cell).
entities.observe: Hurdle fencing the shepherd threw up after the thicket business. Two ewe lambs inside it, and a third that will not put weight on a foreleg.
entities.once_per_waking_toast: The lambs have had their handling for today. Crowd them now and you undo it.
entities.toast: You get a hand under the limping one and hold it until it stops shaking. Fleece comes away on your fingers.

variants.toast: They come to the rail for you now. You work burrs out of three fleeces and leave the bad leg for last.

on_skill_use.toast: [Beast's Mending] — You strap the lamb's leg, and it stands on it before you have finished. The ewes crowd in to look.

entities._comment: #330 R4: the wolf's second cache. Same variant-zeroing shape as its floodplains twin; item yield, no gold.
entities.observe: A scatter of old bones in the field grass, half sunk. The wolf keeps returning to it, head down, digging and stopping and digging again.
entities.toast: The wolf turns up a thin copper ring from under a stone, worn bright on the inside of the band.

variants.toast: Turned earth, filled in and gone quiet. The wolf walks past it now.

entities._comment: [Basic Repair] CARRIER. (19,9) was ALREADY blocked by the cottage block, so it moves no walkability and can persist forever -- which is what lets visual_states show the mend. (20,9) is the cell that opens; face this from (19,10).
entities.observe: Two stringers still run out along the bank from the cottage corner, and the decking between them is gone — lifted by a flood and never replaced. The beams are sound. It is boards it wants.
entities.locked_toast: The stringers are sound and the boards are somewhere downriver. Standing here wishing at it will not deck it.
entities.repair_toast: [Basic Repair] — You cut boards to the span and lay them across the stringers. The walk takes your weight from one end to the other.

entities._comment: The cell the mend opens. The bank walk is one cell wide, so this single blocker IS the detour: 13 steps around, 3 through.
entities.observe: Where the decking used to be there is a scoured trench down to the water, wider than a stride and undercut on both lips.
entities.locked_toast: The bank is cut clean through here, down to brown water. Go the long way round the cottage, or put boards back across it.

entities._comment: [Broader Shoulders] carrier. REPEATABLE (once_per_waking + gold). Sited here, not the north gallery: a trader L2 grant has to be reachable by a trader.
entities.once_per_waking_toast: The dray stands empty and the shed is stacked to the door. The bank head has no more work in it until tomorrow.
entities.observe: Grain sacks off a dray at the bank head, a dozen of them on the boards. Two men stand looking at the stack with their hands on their hips.
entities.locked_toast: The first sack moves. Your back has nothing for the eleven behind it. Shifting a stack like that takes strength you have not learned yet.
entities.skill_hint_toast: Dragging them one at a time will take all day. Carrying them properly would not.

on_skill_use.toast: [Broader Shoulders] — You take three at once and walk them up to the shed without stopping. The dray is clear before the second man has picked up his first, and two coins come your way for it.

entities.toast: You walk the sign back. The pack came off the north ground by the old line — something denned in it and they gave way. They didn't choose these fields. They were pushed.
